components.parameter_and_cost_changes: Dimension one, diameter D, no additional scale restriction on M beyond M>epsilon; zero charged calls in the indistinguishability argument.
components.preserved_model_properties: Both operators are C-infinity on R; their monotonicity pairing and all derivative differences vanish. Lip(D^(p-1)F)=0<=Lp. For distinct points the zero monotonicity pairing rules out every positive strong-monotonicity parameter.
components.transcript_control: At budget zero, H0 is the same empty history and the independent seed produces the same output law for both signs.
components.transformation: Keep the public interval and x0 fixed and use the two constant signs F_+=M and F_-=-M.

construction.definition: In R with Euclidean norm |.|, let a=-D/2, b=D/2, X=[a,b], x0=0. Choose M>epsilon and define globally F_s(x)=s M for s in {+1,-1}. The family contains two fixed operators, not a chain construction. N_X(x)={n:n(z-x)<=0 for all z in X}; r_s(x)=inf_{n in N_X(x)}|s M+n|.
construction.hidden_objects: The sign s is fixed before execution and independent of the algorithm seed. It is inaccessible without operator information. No hidden directions, rotations, chain length or adaptive operator choices are used.

model_membership_refs.scope: Model membership established in the complete local argument: globally smooth constants, monotonicity, derivative Lipschitz constant zero and absence of positive strong monotonicity.

construction.parameters: Every fixed integer p>=2 and every Lp,D,epsilon>0; d=1; any finite M>epsilon, for example M=2epsilon. Diameter(X)=D. Lp is an available upper bound, not the minimum derivative Lipschitz constant.
construction.public_information: Public input (d=1,X=[-D/2,D/2],x0=0,p,Lp,D,epsilon) is identical for both members. The lower bound remains true even if the two-member family and common M are disclosed; the sign remains hidden.

escape_conditions.epistemic_note: Explicit local argument included in the linked theorem; not an upper bound for the entire admissible operator class.
escape_conditions.scope: This two-member family under exact value or full-jet access.
escape_conditions.statement: One feasible value query, for example at x0=0, returns s M and reveals the sign. Return a if the value is positive and b if negative; n=-F_s belongs to the corresponding endpoint normal cone and gives residual zero.

escape_conditions.epistemic_note: Follows directly from the explicit residual and membership calculations.
escape_conditions.scope: Changes to hidden information, parameter regime or model class.
escape_conditions.statement: Public disclosure of s also removes the obstruction. If M<=epsilon, every feasible point already meets the residual tolerance; if a positive strong-monotonicity parameter is required, these instances are excluded.

hardness_claims.algorithm_coverage: Every arbitrary measurable randomized zero-query feasible output rule whose seed is independent of the unknown operator; deterministic rules are included.
hardness_claims.missing_lifting: No lifting needed for this zero-query claim. No N>=1 hardness or epsilon-power lower bound is asserted.
hardness_claims.regime_note: For every fixed p>=2, Lp,D,epsilon>0 and M>epsilon, one fixed member has success probability <=1/2. Hence success >=2/3 on every admissible instance requires at least one oracle call.

oracle_realizations.choices_and_history: The algorithm may use arbitrary measurable internal operations and an independent seed. Query/output rules are total and feasible; there is no span restriction or requirement to query the output. The oracle always evaluates the same fixed F_s.
oracle_realizations.cost: One feasible full-jet evaluation counts as one original-operator call. The hardness claim concerns worst-case budget N=0; internal computation is unrestricted and uncharged in this information model. One value evaluation, already included in one jet call, reveals s.
oracle_realizations.information_bottleneck: With no operator call the common public input and empty history reveal no sign information. There is no remaining information bottleneck after one value query.
oracle_realizations.information_to_error: N_X(a)=(-infinity,0], N_X(b)=[0,infinity), and N_X(x)={0} for a<x<b. Thus r_+(a)=0 and r_+(x)=M at every x!=a; r_-(b)=0 and r_-(x)=M at every x!=b. Since M>epsilon, success requires output exactly a for F_+ and exactly b for F_-. Under the common output law these disjoint events have probabilities summing to at most one.
oracle_realizations.query_and_feedback: At any feasible x in X return O_p^{F_s}(x)=(s M,0,...,0), with all derivatives D^j F_s=0 for 1<=j<=p-1. Multilinear derivatives use the Euclidean operator norm.
oracle_realizations.sampling_and_reuse: Feedback is exact and deterministic conditional on s. Repeated queries return the identical jet. At zero queries H0 is empty for both members; coupling the same independent seed gives identical outputs.

summary: Two admissible one-dimensional constant operators have disjoint singleton tangent-residual solution sets. Any randomized zero-query output has success probability at most 1/2 on one fixed member; one value query completely resolves this family.
title: Opposite constant operators: zero-query Hard Family
use_when: Prove that a uniform tangent-residual oracle budget cannot be zero for any positive Lp,D,epsilon.
Supply the constant-budget obstruction in a normalization argument; do not use this family for positive-budget epsilon-power hardness.
